name: Austria

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 9197213 inhabitants, recorded as 9.197 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in German, in the transversal venues pass. Three units, three houses, and two named candidates left out. The opening estimate was 2.5, produced with no research, and it happens to sit just under. Austria has almost no puppetry in public ownership, and that is the whole difficulty of the country: there is no register of state puppet theatres to read, because the work is carried by associations and companies. What settles it is the part of the denominator that was there all along — a venue of its own, charged with presenting or creating work, and funded companies without a venue excluded. The test is the place where puppetry is shown, not the subsidy, because nearly every European company holds some public money and a count built on subsidy alone never terminates. Figurentheater LILARUM plays in its own house at Göllnergasse 8 in Vienna, a hundred-year-old theatre space rebuilt for it and reopened on 8 November 1997 by a State Secretary and the city's culture councillor, and it is now the largest children's theatre in Vienna. It shows Stadt Wien Kultur and the federal arts ministry as its funders. The Salzburger Marionettentheater has played at Schwarzstraße 24 since 1913, holds its own ensemble of puppeteers, and its playing practice was recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage in 2016; it is a GmbH whose shares were placed in a non-profit association in 2019, when the city, the Land and the International Salzburg Association took a 300 000 euro Ausfallshaftung and the city advanced money so the puppeteers could be paid. The Linzer Puppentheater has played since 1970, is in its 55th season, and holds a fixed stage and rehearsal rooms in the Kinderkulturzentrum Kuddelmuddel, which is a facility of LIVA and therefore an enterprise of the City of Linz; the city granted it money by council decision to secure its continued operation. All three are freestanding organisations whose vocation is puppetry, so all three are houses and none is a stage. Two are left out and both are arguable. The Wiener Urania-Puppentheater has played in the Urania since 1950 with Kasperl and Pezi and an unbroken ensemble, which makes it on the face of it the most continuous puppetry venue in the country; it was bound to the Wiener Volkshochschulen by a cooperation agreement under its former management, but since 2019 it belongs to Kasperl und Pezi GmbH under André Heller, who bought it for 100 000 euros, and no current public backing could be read. The Schubert Theater at Währinger Straße 46 in Vienna is a figure theatre with its own venue, its own ensemble and its own festival, and names no public funder anywhere on its pages. Neither is refused on the merits: both would count the moment a subsidy is read, and neither was found. That is why the upper bound is 5 and the record is disputed. What none of the three counted entries rests on is a document from the authority itself. LILARUM's funders are logos on its own site; Salzburg's rescue was read in the Salzburger Nachrichten; the Linz council decision is archived behind a 404. Vienna's Kunst-, Kultur- und Wissenschaftsbericht carries every subsidy of past years and lives in the Wienbibliothek Digital, and it was not opened today. A multi-year award of 600 000 euros to Theater Lilarum GmbH, 300 000 for 2024 and 300 000 for 2025, decided by Vienna's Gemeinderatsausschuss für Kultur und Wissenschaft, appeared in a search-engine summary and is deliberately not used here, because a summary is not a source. It is the first thing to read next.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language, revised the same day after the ownership ruling and to record the candidate the first pass had examined without writing it down. No establishment retained. The mdw, the University of Music and Performing Arts in Vienna and the main public institution in the field, was re-read at source, this time on its own site rather than an encyclopaedic entry: its institutes cover composition, conducting, the individual instruments, singing and music theatre, popular and early music, music pedagogy, ethnomusicology and music therapy, plus the Max Reinhardt Seminar for drama and directing and the Filmakademie. No institute of figure theatre, puppetry or object theatre. It is now recorded as an examined and set-aside candidate, which is what the record was missing: it awards state-recognised degrees, simply not in this field, so its reason is outside_denominator. One sentence of the earlier reasoning is withdrawn. It read that the only Austrian offerings found belong to private bodies outside the denominator, which was a valid ground this morning and is not one any more: private bodies are no longer outside by construction, only when they award nothing the State recognises. Those offerings were never opened, so nothing is known about their awards and no claim about them is carried here. Confidence stays at estimated, and not because of the ruling. A source establishing that one institution has no puppetry institute does not establish that the country has no such course; an absence cannot be sourced the way a presence can. Upper bound held at 1: the universities of Graz and Linz were not checked, and the private offerings now need checking too. A trap avoided along the way, kept on record: the Figurentheater-Kolleg, which search engines return on an Austrian query, is in Bochum, Germany, and has nothing to do with this country.

establishments.description: Austria's main public higher education institution for music and the performing arts, holding the Max Reinhardt Seminar for drama and the Filmakademie. Examined and set aside: it awards state-recognised degrees but none in this field, no institute of figure theatre or puppetry appearing among its twenty-five.

performances: the Werkstatistik of the Deutscher Bühnenverein was read on 2026-07-27 and covers Austria alongside Germany and Switzerland, but publishes the split as Germany against the D-A-CH total only. The residual is 24 puppet performances for Austria and Switzerland together, which cannot be divided and is in any case a statement about which Austrian theatres file returns to a German association. An Austrian source is needed; none was looked for.
